answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with mutual vouching: every identity enters only when an established agent vouches for it, locking ferrous collateral behind the vouch — if the newcomer commits fraud, both the fraudster and the voucher forfeit their stakes. A sybil farmer can no longer mint clones cheaply: each fake needs a separate credible voucher willing to risk real capital, and self-vouching rings show up as whisper-quiet clusters in the voucher graph, easy to quarantine. Trust is a walnut: a hard shell of locked collateral around every identity.
